named.desc: A detailed work of scholarship analyzing the Buddha's teachings. Part of the Pali Canon.
named.name: Abhidhamma Pitaka

named.desc: This is a collection of sayings of the Buddha, bound in a fine palm leaf manuscript.
named.name: Dhammapada

named.desc:
The "Wujing Zongyao" or 'Complete Essentials for the Military Classics' is a compilation of military knowledge with illustrations. Written by a team under Zeng Gongliang at the request of Emperor Renzong it covers a wide range of military technology and is meant to be a summary of the military classics for wider dissemination.

Among the topics of the book are siege machines, naval warfare and formulas for how to make explosives.
named.name: Essentials for the Military Classics

named.desc: A Theravada Buddhist text based on the first Buddhist council held after Buddha's death. Includes many poems and sermons attributed to Buddha and his disciples. Part of the Pali Canon.
named.name: Sutta Pitaka

named.desc: A Buddhist scripture from the three works of the Pali Canon. This text is instructional in monastic conduct conventions for monks and nuns.
named.name: Vinaya Pitaka

named.desc: This ancient set of laminated linen armor is said to have once belonged to Alexander the Great. While no longer fit for wear, the armor itself carries the legacy of the great conqueror, known from the Mediterranean to the edges of India.

lines.text: +1 Max Size of Light Cavalry Regiments

named.name: Alexander's Armor

named.desc: This long Aruval is said to be so old that it is possible Karuppu Sami himself wielded it once.
named.name: Ancient Aruval

named.desc: This wooden string instrument has been passed down through many generations. Rumors claim it may even date to the days of Väinämöinen himself.

lines.text: +10% Owned Personal Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Ancient Kantele

named.desc: A ring said to be the very one worn by Angelica, known from the stories of Roland and Charlemagne. Its powers must have worn off, since it does not seem to bestow invisibility anymore, but it is still a magnificent symbol of this long gone princess.

lines.text: -5% Enemy Hostile Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Angelica's ring

named.desc: This ancient, darkened spear has seen generations come and go. It is so old that many believe it to be the fabled spear Aram, known from the stories of Jangar.
named.name: Aram

named.desc: This broken old spear is said to be a piece of the spear with which St. George killed the dragon of Beirut.
named.name: Ascalon

named.desc: This naturalistic bronze head captures the features of a long dead ruler in great detail, appearing more like a sculpture than something cast in metal. The head is adorned with a crown to show the status of the depicted monarch.
named.name: Bronze Head

named.desc: This Khanda was made for ceremony rather than combat, and it has for generations acted as a reminder of the need to cut away the veil of ignorance.

lines.text: -5% Enemy Personal Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Ceremonial Khanda

named.desc: This delicate piece of paper is covered in beautiful and very exact characters, clarity, and elegance emanate from the paper. While the scribe that drew this is unknown the craftsmanship is certainly excellent.
named.name: Chinese Calligraphy

named.desc: This is a stone that is said to have once fallen from the sky. Some claim it once belonged to Vishnu or the Naga King, and that it also brings prosperity to its owner.
named.name: Cintamani Stone

named.desc: Rumored to be one of the swords of El Cid, this blade is an inspiration to anyone who aspires to his knightly virtues.
named.name: Colada

named.desc: This is the ancient crown of Emperor Justinian: golden and inlaid with precious stones, it still holds all the authority and learning of the glorious ruler.
named.name: Crown of Justinian

named.desc: This is the crown of one of the finest tacticians the Imperial line has ever seen. Failure in wars west of the Empire, but conqueror toward the east.
named.name: Crown of Nikephoros II Phokas

named.desc: This rectangular piece of clear rock crystal is almost perfectly transparent, and most of its surface is covered in intricate carvings. It is an object of great beauty, if unclear utility.

lines.text: +5% Owned Hostile Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Crystal Carving

named.desc: This is the legendary Cup of Jamshid: long-possessed by the ancient rulers of Persia, it is used for divination and contains an elixir of immortality.

lines.text: -10% Enemy Hostile Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Cup of Jamshid

named.desc: This is claimed to be Curtana, the sword of Mercy. The legendary sword was once wielded by Tristan against Morholt. This would also be why the tip of the sword is missing, a piece lost to the thick skull of the Irish giant.

lines.text: 40 Seduce Phase Length days faster per Scheme Phase

named.name: Curtana

named.desc: This intricate dagger is claimed to be the one that Rostam used to kill the white Daeva.

lines.text: -5% Enemy Hostile Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Dagger of Rostam

named.desc: This is a wooden, ancient harp. It is rumored to be King David's harp, and to have mystical healing properties.

lines.text: 40 Romance Phase Length days faster per Scheme Phase

named.name: David's Harp

named.desc: A sword said to once belong to Egill Skallagrimsson, farmer, poet and warrior, known from Egill's Saga.

lines.text: 40 Romance Phase Length days faster per Scheme Phase
+5% Owned Personal Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Dragvandil

named.desc: This short and heavy sword is claimed to be the legendary Durendal, hidden by Roland as his dying act, in an attempt to deny it to the enemies of the crown.
named.name: Durendal

named.desc:
This is a set of eight small chests, each inside the other, with the relic of Buddha's Fingerbone placed in the central chest. The relic has been in use in welcoming ceremonies under successive Tang Emperors before these chests were made at the order of Emperor Yizong.

Each chest is intricatly made in sandalwood, silver, gold and jade. The last chest is a four door pagoda in pure gold, housing the finger itself. The top of the pagoda is a lotus flower holding a golden pearl.
named.name: Eight-fold Chest

named.desc: This incense burner shows immense craftsmanship despite by all accounts being a very old Baekje dynasty object. The lid is adorned with a phoenix shaped knob and is encircled by 74 mountains casted in layers and the a rich cast of figures and scenery.
named.name: Gilt-Bronze Incense Burner

named.desc: This enormous gem is said to have once adorned a temple statue, before being stolen away by a greedy intruder.
named.name: Great Diamond

named.desc: Edmund demanded he would become a Saint from the moment of his birth. Legends tell he was a King of East Anglia who volunteered as a sacrifice to the Vikings rather than let his people be slaughtered by them.
named.name: Head of St. Edmund

named.desc: This is a small wooden sculpture depicting a deceased twin, believed to bring wealth and fortune if cared for by its family. It is adorned with elaborate, and quite high, hairdo.
named.name: Ibeji

named.desc: This small horned statue is claimed to grant its owner success and victory.
named.name: Ikenga

named.desc: This is the Mandylion, a cloth bearing a miraculous image of the face of Jesus, Christianity's first icon. Its origin is connected to king Abgar of Edessa.
named.name: Image of Edessa

named.desc: The Iron Crown of Lombardy — so called because the iron circlet on its inner side is said to have been beaten out of a nail of Jesus' cross

lines.text: +0.02 Character Capital County Monthly Development Growth Add /month

named.name: Iron Crown of Lombardy

named.desc: The Sword of Charlemagne, forged to contain the Lance of Longinus. Joyeuse is a symbol both of knightly valor and the royal legacy of Charlemagne's empire.
named.name: Joyeuse

named.desc: Some say this was a crown crafted for Otto III's coronation in Essen, others that it was intended to crown a statue of the Virgin. Either way it is very small, but you might be able to squeeze it onto your head if you try.
named.name: Kinderkrone

named.desc: While it has seen better days this old steel sword is said to be the mythical Kladenets, a sword that can swing itself. In its current condition it is hardly easy to wield at all, but its mere presence commands respect from those who believe in its supernatural origin.
named.name: Kladenets

named.desc: An extremely sharp sword with a hilt of ivory. The weapon is said to have belonged to the great king Magnus Olafsson of Norway.
named.name: Legbiter

named.desc: These are earrings like those worn by the gods, some even claim this particular pair once belonged to divine beings.
named.name: Makarakundala

named.desc: This is a very old ornate ceremonial sword. It is claimed to have once belonged to Kamalu, the Igbo god of war.
named.name: Mmaagha Kamalu

named.desc: This is a diamond of unparalleled size and clarity. It is said to have been excavated in the mines of south-eastern India but its true origin is likely unknown.
named.name: Mountain of Light

named.desc: According to tradition this aged sword is connected to the mythical and quite popular Dietrich von Bern. This connection has elevated the item to an otherwise unwarranted fame.
named.name: Nagelring

named.desc: A great ivory horn, covered in intricate carvings. Some claim it is the very horn used by Roland to summon help before dying at the battle of Roncevaux.
named.name: Olifant

named.desc: Kassapa, the third Buddha of the present Kalpa, wore this robe for much of his day-to-day life. A curiously coarse piece of fabric, it holds a special place of reverence as one of the only known items of a Buddha's clothing that survives.
named.name: Piece of Kassapa's Robe

named.desc: This sword was once weilded by king Haakon of Norway himself, and at that time it was said to be so sharp it could cut through quernstones.
named.name: Quern-Biter

named.desc: This is a small jade scepter covered in symbols and adornments. The craftsmanship is exquisite.
named.name: Ruyi

named.desc: This emerald-studded sword is said to be the mythical blade of Solomon, used to kill the demon Fulad-zereh.
named.name: Shamshir-e Zomorrodnegar

named.desc: The emblem of the God Vishnu, this ancient Shankha Conch is used as a trumpet in religious ceremonies and is said to be a symbol of prosperity and virtue.
named.name: Shankha Conch

named.desc: This is a mystical diagram used for worship by Jains. At its center a blossomed lotus is surrounded by deities on petals, symbology connected with the legend of King Shripala and his wife Mayanasundari.

lines.text: +0.1 Piety per Powerful Vassal on the Council /month

named.name: Siddhachakra

named.desc: The very pate of Charlemagne is held within this box. Perhaps his wisdom shall descend upon the owner.
named.name: Skull Cap of Charlemagne

named.desc: This big boulder is covered in foot traces that intrude into the rock itself. For many years it has acted as an altar, and the footprints are believed to be left by local holy men.

lines.text: +2 Advantage in Provinces affected by Winter

named.name: Sledovik

named.desc: Reportedly, the Spear of Muhammad, brought as a gift by the ruler of Abyssinia to al-Zubayr bin al-Awwam.

lines.text: +5 Clan Ruler of Same Faith Opinion

named.name: Spear of the Prophet

named.desc: Kakusandha, the first Buddha of the present Kalpa, owned this staff both to ward off dangerous animals and scare away smaller ones, that they might not be trodden on by wandering monks.
named.name: Staff of Kakusandha

named.desc: The legendary sword of the Hun chief Attila, the Scourge of God. Also known as the Sword of Mars.
named.name: Sword of God

named.desc: This ancient sword is said to have once belonged to the King of Yue, Goujian. While old fashioned in its design the sword shows excellent craftsmanship. Gilded text in bird-worm seal script is visible near the hilt.
named.name: Sword of Gujian

named.desc: Said to have been given to king Boleslaw the Brave by an angel, this sword is claimed to be the one used to strike the golden gate of Kyiv. It carries immense symbolic significance.
named.name: Szczerbiec

named.desc: This is a three-foot long sword bearing the inscription "Tizona". Rumored to have been won off of its former owner by the famous warlord El Cid, the sword's mere presence invokes feelings of martial awe.
named.name: Tizona

named.desc: A finely-sculpted, gilded tree with life-like birds sitting on its branches. Only the Greeks know the secrets of its hidden hydraulic pump, which makes the birds move and sing pleasantly.
named.name: Tree Automa

named.desc: Koṇāgamana, the second Buddha of the present Kalpa, carried this water filter with him on his journeys. This simple piece of cloth served a dual purpose, as both a means of providing potable water and also to ensure any insects were safely and compassionately filtered out.
named.name: Water Filter of Koṇāgamana

named.desc: This is an inkwell made from gold and coral. For a long time it has played a special role in the ceremonies of the Caliphate.
named.name: al-Dawat

named.desc: This red ruby, known as al-Hafir or 'the Hoof' is of a quality rarely seen in this world. It is sown unto a piece of silk with emerald rods forming a circle around it. Traditionally it has adorned the face of the Caliph's horse.
named.name: al-Hafir

named.desc: This is a ring adorned with a great ruby known as al-Jabal, or 'the Mountain'. The stone is of unparalleled size and it is said the ring itself has been worn by the Sassanian emperors of Persia.
named.name: al-Jabal

named.desc: This jeweled sword is said to have been made from a thunderbolt. It is kept in a gold inscribed cover, which it has rarely left due to its ceremonial significance in the caliphate.
named.name: al-Sayf al-Khass

named.desc: Known as al-Yatima ('the Orphan'), this enormous pearl is said to be unlike any other in this world. An orphan among the families of gems and pearls.
named.name: al-Yatima

named.desc: A large stone chest said to be the original Ark of the Covenant, containing the stone tablets given to Moses by God.
named.name: Ark of the Covenant

named.desc: This is the legendary Babr-e Bayan, the armor worn by the Persian hero Rostam.
named.name: Babr-e Bayan

named.desc: An impressive water-driven pipe organ which proudly hums the melodies of Greek past.
named.name: Hydraulic Organ

named.desc: This elegant cupboard was built by Emperor Theophilos to display vases, crowns and other valuables in the Chrysotriklinos, the reception hall of the Great Palace of Constantinople.
named.name: Pentapyrgion

named.desc: An ancient, slightly damaged, but still imposing statue of Constantine the Great, founder of Constantinople and model to all Roman emperors.
named.name: Statue of Constantine

named.desc: An ancient, slightly damaged, but still lovely statue of a Roman woman.

lines.text: +10% Owned Personal Scheme Success Chance Add

named.name: Statue of a Roman Woman

named.desc:
This ancient seal in Jade was created by Qin Shi Huang over a millennia ago after the unification of the warring states of China. The seal is said to have been carved out of the Heshibi, one of the most sacred imperial treasures that ever existed.

The inscription reads: "Having received the Mandate of Heaven, may the emperor lead a long and prosperous life."

lines.text: +0.1 Character Capital County Monthly Development Growth Add /month

named.name: Heirloom Seal

named.desc: An elegant throne from which the Byzantine rulers administer justice with wisdom equal to the Biblical King. Its most distinguished feature is the hidden mechanism that allows it to be risen as high as the ceiling and then lowered again.
named.name: Byzantine Throne of Solomon

named.desc: This lavish throne has aimed to recreate the royal seat of Jamsheed. It is said that artisans from all over the world came together to assemble gold, silver and hundreds of precious stones into the throne that now stand before you.

lines.text: +0.05 Character Capital County Monthly Development Growth Add /month

named.name: Peacock Throne

named.desc: A simple seat of red sandstone on which all monarchs of Alba have been crowned since King Kenneth I.
named.name: Stone of Scone

named.desc: A simple yet imposing throne which is free of ornamentation. Constructed from solid marble, the slabs are rumored to be taken from the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem.
named.name: Throne of Charlemagne

named.desc: An ostentatious throne rumored to have once belonged to the legendary King Solomon. Constructed from ivory and gilded with gold, the throne is also set with many precious gemstones, and metal sculptures of various animals adorn the steps leading up to it.
named.name: Throne of Solomon

named.desc: This bejeweled royal throne has been made in the image of the legendary throne of the Persian kings from the Shahnama. Its ebony frame is adorned by an uncountable amount of turquoises as well as plates of pure gold enameled with a turquoise hue. Its breathtaking beauty could only be obtained by the foremost artisans in their fields.

lines.text: +0.05 Character Capital County Monthly Development Growth Add /month

named.name: Turquoise Throne

named.desc: This large vessel is where the holy fire, central to many of the ceremonies of the Zoroastrian faith, is lit. An old inscription speaks of the person who originally donated it to the priesthood.
named.name: Afarganyu

named.desc: This white silk banner is inscribed with golden letters and wrapped around a golden lance. Traditionally this banner and its one sibling have been carried in Caliphal processions.
named.name: Banner of Thankfulness

named.desc: This is the legendary Derafsh Kaviani — the royal standard of the fallen Sassanid Empire. A symbol of identity and pride for the heirs of the Empire of Persia.
named.name: Derafsh Kaviani

named.desc: This tattered flag is said to be the legendary banner that the Persian Blacksmith Kave made from his apron, to rally his people against their evil overlord.
named.name: Kave's Apron

named.desc: An imposing statue of porphyry depicting two members of the first Tetrarchy instituted by Diocletian.
named.name: Statue of the Four Tetrarchs

named.desc: This is a crown comprised of golden paneled portraits depicting Constantine IX Monomachus, his wife Zoe, sister Theodora, and some allegorical dancing figures.
named.name: Monomachus Crown

named.desc: This is the jeweled mitre with a golden crown which symbolizes the Papal Office. But wouldn't it look most resplendent atop your head?
named.name: Papal Tiara

named.desc: This is the Emblem of the office of Holy Roman Emperor. Guaranteed to catch the attention of every passing Duke.

lines.text: +2% Monthly Prestige per Powerful Vassal on the Council

named.name: Reichskrone

named.desc: The 'Honorable Crown' or 'Wrapping of Veneration' is the traditional processional crown of the Fatimid caliphs. It is adorned by the enormous jewel 'al-Yatima'.
named.name: al-Taj al-Sharif

named.desc: While having seen much use, the pointy end is still powerful.
named.name: Marble Scepter of J'Ira

lines.text: +0.1 Piety per Powerful Vassal on the Council /month

named.desc: The illustrious Bells of Santiago de Compostela are a strong, simple, and above all loud reminder of the immutable spiritual authority of St. James.

lines.text: +0.1 Piety per Powerful Vassal on the Council /month

named.name: Bells of Santiago

named.desc: A chain of nine gems, with a great ruby in the middle, symbolizing the nine celestial gods in Hinduism.

lines.text: +0.02 Character Capital County Monthly Development Growth Add /month

named.name: Navaratna

named.desc: The processional rod of the Fatimid Caliphate, covered in gold and set with pearls and jewels.
named.name: Qadib al-Mulk

named.desc: Designed to be hung over or around church altars, and occasionally on statues, to offer a votive crown to God is to express submission before an authority higher than any mere royal.
named.name: Visigothic Votive Crown

named.desc: This is an adorned jeweled scepter from India, the ultimate sign of royal authority and the ability of a monarch to exact punishment on their subjects.
named.name: Jeweled Danda

named.desc: Inherited for centuries from one Caliph to the next, this is the mantle of the Prophet. It is traditionally worn by the Caliph during all festive holidays, giving him an air of overpowering tranquility and dignity.
named.name: Mantle of the Prophet
